newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Sparks says China may export 3 mln T maize 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Sparks says China may export 3 mln T maize 1996/97.

text.p: China may export 3.0 million tonnes of 1996/97 maize and 1.5 million tonnes in 1997/98, while U.S. exports should rise to 50.8 million tonnes in 1997/98 from 45.7 million tonnes, Sparks Companies said Monday.

U.S. 1997 maize output should be about 243.5 million tonnes. This is based on estimated sown area of 32.9 million hectares, average yields of 8.0 tonnes and harvesting of 92.2 percent of sown area, U.S. agricultural consultant Sparks Companies of Memphis, Tenn. said in a report released at a conference in Buenos Aires.
These and other market factors "suggest that future prices of December maize should be in the range of $2.40 and $2.65 during the October to December quarter," Sparks added.

The report said, "China has accumulated an export surplus after two good maize harvests in a row and hopes to export 3.0 million tonnes in 1996/97. It will also probably be a net exporter of 1.5 million tonnes during 1997/98."
It added that Sparks "estimates that demand for residual and forrage maize will be moderate during 1997/98, reaching levels more consistent with supply and the price of the grain."
